answer: A refundable stake is an anti-Sybil defense: each agent must lock collateral before transacting, so a thousand fake identities require a thousand stakes. Like a ridge that must be climbed before every crossing, the deposit raises the price of each new identity while honest agents recover theirs after a verifiable work period. An attacker cannot hide on an island of fake accounts either: attestations are public, and correlated identities are slashed together, forfeiting every stake at once. This turns Sybil attacks into a losing trade, with no ivory tower of paperwork — only measurable cost.
